title: Man asked to be shot in July standoff with police
article: Trevor Colin Graham had an armed confrontation with police several months before he was shot and killed by an officer during a drugstore robbery in Kitchener last week.

Then living in Paris, Ont., under the terms of a conditional sentence, Graham was described as "drunk and out of control" by the Ontario Provincial Police after they were called to his home by his mother on July 31.
A police report on the 11:30 p.m. incident said Graham had locked himself inside the house, was armed with a knife and had slashed his wrists and arms numerous times.
He was alternately belligerent and calm with police, yelling profanities, waving the knife back and forth, taunting officers or asking them for cigarettes.
At one point, according to the report, Graham "yelled at an officer that he wanted him to shoot him in the head."
Graham eventually calmed down and unlocked the door. He was taken to hospital by ambulance for treatment of the slashes on his arms.
The OPP report, part of a court file in Brantford, said police seized three knives from the home, which had been "trashed" by Graham.
At the time, Graham was serving an eight-month conditional sentence for breach of probation and being an accessory to a robbery at a Brantford coffee shop.
After the July 31 incident, he was taken into custody and charged with weapons offences and breaching his conditional sentence by drinking and failing to keep the peace.
His mother, Karyn Graham, and a close friend have said he remained in a Brantford jail until three days before he was shot once in the chest by a Waterloo regional police officer on Nov. 20.
Graham, 26, was fleeing the Shoppers Drug Mart store in the Sunrise Centre with stolen prescription drugs when he was confronted by two uniformed officers in a vestibule at the front entrance.
A civilian agency investigating his death has not said if Graham was armed or what happened in the exchange with officers before he was killed.
Karyn Graham has said her son, originally from the Hamilton area, was a troubled man who had battled depression and drug addiction for years.
He was nearing the end of methadone treatment for an addiction to the painkiller OxyContin, she said, and hoped to become a heavy equipment operator after earning a high school diploma in jail.
Karyn Graham said he was in good spirits and showed no signs of drug abuse just hours before he was killed at the Ottawa Street South store.
The store is located near the Kitchener house where Graham was staying with his mother and her boyfriend after getting out of jail on Nov. 17.
